name: Daridorexant

lead: Daridorexant (Quviviq) is a prescription sleep medicine for adults with insomnia. People interested in looks follow it because deeper, longer sleep is linked with clearer skin, less puffiness and a fresher face.

It works by blocking orexin receptors OX1R and OX2R, which turns down the brain's wake signal rather than boosting GABA. Two phase 3 trials examined night-time and daytime insomnia symptoms; appearance has not been a studied outcome.

paras: It is taken as a prescribed nightly tablet by adults diagnosed with insomnia, usually as part of a broader sleep routine. People who use it for recovery describe the aim as more consistent sleep, with any change in skin or facial freshness following over weeks of better rest.

Reported effects include sleepiness and headache. The label warns about next-day impairment, sleep paralysis, complex sleep behaviors and mood effects. It is prescription-only and a Schedule IV controlled substance in the US.

angle.text: Daridorexant is a prescription orexin-blocking sleep drug (Quviviq). The idea is deeper, longer sleep leading to better overnight recovery, which shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It has been studied in insomnia trials.

lead: Daridorexant, sold as Quviviq, is a prescription dual orexin receptor antagonist for adults with insomnia involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep. It was developed by Idorsia Pharmaceuticals and was formerly known as nemorexant during development.[1]

Grokipedia reports FDA approval on 7 January 2022 and European Medicines Agency approval on 29 April 2022, making it the third orexin receptor antagonist approved for insomnia after suvorexant and lemborexant.[1][2] Two phase 3 trials examined both night-time and daytime symptoms of insomnia.[3]

It has no approved or studied appearance indication. Its connection to looksmaxxing is limited to general conversation about sleep and recovery. Reported adverse effects include somnolence and headache, and the label warns of next-day impairment and complex sleep behaviors.[4]

paras: The label indicates daridorexant for adults with insomnia characterised by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance.[4] European guidelines discuss orexin antagonists among the pharmacological options for insomnia.[5] No cosmetic or appearance use is approved or has been studied.

Daridorexant blocks both orexin receptors, OX1R and OX2R, reducing the wake-promoting effect of orexin neuropeptides made in the hypothalamus.[4][1] This differs from benzodiazepines and Z-drugs, which act on GABA-A receptors.[1] It is primarily metabolised by CYP3A4, and the label addresses use with CYP3A4 inhibitors and in hepatic impairment.[4][1]

Grokipedia lists somnolence and headache as common effects and notes rarer risks including complex sleep behaviors, sleep paralysis, hallucinations and next-day impairment.[1] The label includes warnings on CNS-depressant effects, sleep paralysis and cataplexy-like symptoms, complex sleep behaviors, respiratory function and worsening depression or suicidal ideation, and the drug is Schedule IV in the US.[4][1]

Two multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials at 156 sites in 17 countries assessed safety and efficacy on night-time and daytime insomnia symptoms.[3] A separate trial studied older adults with insomnia disorder, and a long-term study reported safety and tolerability data.[6][7] A narrative review describes the drug's pharmacology and trial programme.[8] Grokipedia summarises trials as showing reductions in wake after sleep onset and increases in total sleep time versus placebo.[1]

Network meta-analyses and guidelines place orexin antagonists among treatment options for insomnia, with comparisons across drug classes.[9][5] Registered studies include trials in people with insomnia and nocturia and a dose-finding study in adolescents.[10][11] No studies have examined appearance outcomes.
Daridorexant is marketed as Quviviq in several countries.[1] It does not feature prominently in looksmaxxing communities.
